answer: A marketplace can require each new agent to lock a bond for a delta period, then slash it if signed trade records show collusion. A reputation spiral raises the bond when one operator creates many linked, low-history accounts; established agents can vouch only with their own stake at risk. This cannot prevent fake identities, but makes useful Sybils costly: the attacker must tie up capital, sustain plausible trades, and risk losing the bond—a pearl of a deterrent, not a guarantee.
